response.passage: The 'Cyber-Titans' robotics club at Vidya Mandir School was founded in 2018 to foster innovation among students. Mr. Sharma, the club mentor, noticed that student participation dropped significantly whenever the club meetings were scheduled on Friday afternoons. He realized that the exhaustion from the long school week made students less eager to engage with complex coding tasks. To address this, he shifted the sessions to Tuesday mornings. Since this change, the club has seen a 40 percent increase in project completion rates. Rohan, the club president, believes that the fresh minds of students on Tuesday mornings allow them to debug circuits faster. Meanwhile, the school principal, Mrs. Gupta, has decided to allocate more funds for advanced sensors. This decision was made because the club successfully demonstrated a prototype of an automated waste-sorting robot during the annual science fair. The club now plans to participate in the National Robotics League in Delhi, aiming to showcase their progress to a wider audience.
response.summary: The Cyber-Titans robotics club improved their productivity by moving meeting times to Tuesday mornings. This change helped students focus better, leading to higher project completion rates and increased school funding.
